﻿Brand Guidelines﻿

Color

Our brand color palette is centered around Cash Green, a bold distillation of how we redefine money. Though one singular color, our usage of green pushes boundaries, from simple and straightforward, to textured and sensorial.

Cash Green

Cash Green should be omnipresent across all brand touchpoints and used strategically such that it stands out as the hero color. Floods of green can be powerful, but that shouldn't be the only way green shows up, Cash Green’s inclusion should be done thoughtfully and intentionally. Challenge yourself to meet this criteria in unexpected ways. Consider materiality, lighting, props, and styling as avenues to explore, and approach Cash Green with nuance and refinement.

Supporting colors

Black and white provide balance to Cash Green, helping maintain visual clarity and avoid overuse of our signature color. They bring structure and contrast to compositions, allowing green to stand out where it matters most. Citron can be used sparingly as a high-impact accent to introduce depth and energy—but should never be used as a full background fill.

Color Modes

No color system can perfectly represent the full extent of what we see with our eyes in the wider world. Different color modes serve different purposes depending on medium. RGB and Pantone offer the most vibrant on-screen color, while CMYK is used for print, with some limitations in vibrancy and range.

Accessibility

Good accessibility starts with legible text. In digital design, this means ensuring strong contrast between text and background colors. Cash App follows WCAG guidelines, aiming for AAA compliance—the highest standard. This means a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 for normal text to ensure maximum readability.

 

Cash Green is specifically created to work with black text, not green text. Avoid using Cash Green as a critical design element where contrast requirements are not met.

Incorrect Usage

Don’t use the wrong color

Don’t use colors that are obviously not part of the CashApp color palette — brown, mint green, golf green, and so on.

Don’t substitute Cash Green

Use only the Cash Green provided unless you have a specific UI or accessibility need.

Don’t eyedrop CMYK or RGB / Hex values

Small color shifts in RGB can cause headaches for developers. Using the wrong CMYK values can cause unexepected results in print. 

Don’t make muddy gradients

Gradients should be bright. If you are using gradients, make sure they do not turn brown or grey in between the start and end colors.

Don’t forget Cash Green for 

external facing brand applications

Cash Green should be present in most circumstances where color ambiguity would hinder brand recognition.

Don’t use the wrong color mode

Use RGB for screens, CMYK and Pantone for print. Using the wrong color modes will cause serious consistency problems.
